items.fact: A disc pattern projected widefield through the objective bleaches a column through the chamber only at low magnification, large discs or thin chambers. At 40x to 100x, a disc of 1 to 10 um radius in a chamber 30 um deep or more bleaches a slab a few disc radii thick, with 0.015 to 0.46 of a column's contrast.

items.fact: For a camera that weighs every depth equally, the depth-averaged bleach profile evolving by 2-D diffusion is exact, not an approximation, because integrating the 3-D diffusion equation over depth between no-flux walls gives 2-D diffusion. With the camera's own depth selectivity and beads diffusing in and out of the plane it sees, the fitted D moves by less than a factor of two (about 0.47 to 0.65 at high magnification).

items.fact: sim-20260930-401's single-curve threshold of about 300 beads in the disc counted beads through the whole chamber depth. Only the bleached slab carries the signal while every bead in the column adds noise, so the count that matters is the column's count times the contrast squared: about 100x the beads where the contrast is 0.1, and 10,000x where it is 0.01. Its diffusivity, its timing limits and the direction of its soft-edge bias stand; defocus computed directly gives about 2x low, the low end of the 2-4x it named.

items.fact: A sharpness-maximum focus search on a uniform suspension of 100 nm beads has no maximum inside the chamber: every interior plane holds the same in-focus count and the same out-of-focus haze. Beads stuck to the glass make one; from 20x up, at a volume fraction of 1e-6 and a 10 ms frame, 0.8 to 8 stuck beads per 100 um x 100 um field outnumber the free beads in focus, and the number scales with the volume fraction. Beads stuck to both surfaces give two equal peaks a chamber depth apart, by construction.

items.fact: In transmitted light a 5 um polystyrene bead in water is a ball lens: its contrast is least at its own centre plane and greatest either side, and it focuses light to a bright point about 8 um beyond its centre. A peak-brightness focus metric can lock onto that point and a gradient metric sees two peaks either side of the bead.

items.fact: Near a flat coverslip a 5 um bead's diffusion along the wall is halved once its centre is below about 3 um (a gap of about 0.5 um) and reduced tenfold only in contact; toward the wall it is halved below 5.3 um. In an overdamped double well residence times and transition rates scale with the drag, so the bulk model's timescales are 2x too short below about 3 um. A 5 um bead left free settles to a gap of about 0.2 um and moves along the glass at about 0.4 of the bulk rate.

items.fact: After the bleach only the camera's focus matters. At high magnification it must stay within about 3 um of the bleach plane for the fit to stay within a factor of 2, and the focus drift rate that uses that up within the shortest record the fit allows ranges from about 0.06 um/s (a 30 um disc at high magnification, records of about 500 s) to about 50 um/s (small discs at 4x).
